rationale: The two conditioning terms (NEG(pi/at) and NEG(txt/at)) are mechanically near-redundant — tax expense is largely a function of pretax income — so the "tax-loss state" collapses into a low-profitability double-count, making this a cosmetic reweighting of the archive's already-tested Cash-Flow-Strained Capex Acceleration rather than a distinct mechanism.

This is a within-family reshuffle of the archive's Liquidity-Stressed Acquisition Spend — dlc/act is a subcomponent of the already-used lct/act, and negative sales growth was already tested as a distress leg in Distress Hiring Mismatch — so it is unlikely to deliver economically distinct information.

The main effect (change in non-goodwill intangible intensity) is a genuinely new investment channel relative to the archive's goodwill-level signal and the hypothesis matches the expression's sign, though COALESCE(intan,0)/COALESCE(gdwl,0) conflates true zeros with missing data and will create a large mass point that should be diagnosed alongside coverage.

Multiplying the inventory rank by a 0/1 current-deficit indicator zeroes out most of the cross-section, producing massive ties and a degenerate long leg — an unstable portfolio construction rather than a real refinement of the already-tested Inventory Liquidity Trap.

This is close to a rediscovery of the archive's failed Resilient Capex Retrenchment (low capex × improving fundamentals), and the archive's Deferred Maintenance Distress already showed low capex earning positive alpha even in the distress state, suggesting the resilience interaction adds nothing beyond a low-capex main effect; the hypothesis also mislabels DELTA(ib/at) as "operating" profitability.

Scaling equity issuance by real investment outlay is a genuinely distinct financing-versus-investment construct not yet in the archive and is internally consistent with the negative sign, but the ratio has a near-zero/zero denominator problem that 1% winsorization will not fully tame, and it partially overlaps the known external-financing/net-issuance anomaly.
